verdicts.ground: (2)+(3), CONFIRMED by execution: metrics.mjs:84 defines the metric as `ss.length>=2 && /^(That|This|It|Which)\b/.test(ss[1])` — a syntactic test on the second sentence's first word that cannot tell a gloss from an undo path. Run over R10's four HEAD source files (468 rows against the probe's 505, rate 0.066 against 0.063), 31 hits, of which 23 (74%) name an undo, revert or option path — "It can be undone with the map undo." (11), "It can be undone with Undo last pulse.", "It can be reverted to the raw text.", "It can be reversed with Revert a manual edit." — and the remaining 8 are also mechanism sentences ("It can be reloaded from the cloud."). CC-12 licenses exactly these, forbids cutting them, uses the map-undo sentence as its own worked example, and then sets SIZE 0.063 → ≤0.024, which needs ~20 of the 31 gone. The only two routes are deleting licensed undo paths or moving the second sentence's opening word ("The map undo reverses it.") — U4's failure mode. The stated guard ("U9 executed per entry") is a human review living outside the instrument the size is stated against. Also (1): the components (Wolfe 10, Hobb 4, Le Guin 8, ai 14, Kay 3) sum to 39, not the printed 38.
verdicts.cure: Withdraw the size. Either hold R10's rate and print "none measured" until a classifier exists that exempts a second sentence naming a registry field, or re-measure the rate with the undo/option family excluded and set any size against that number.

Second defect in the same rule: CC-13 cites "dnd-flavor 0.021" for the abstract closer, but primary/dnd-flavor.fingerprint.json gives abstractNounRate 0.077 — 0.0213 is that column's PRONOUN closer rate — and §2's own table prints 0.077, so the file carries two numbers for one quantity and argues the size from the wrong one.
